subject: DPA negotiation: data transfers, subprocessors, and TOMs exhibit edits

Subject: Re: DPA negotiation: data transfers, subprocessors, and TOMs exhibit edits

Hi Ava / Marissa,

Thanks for sending the draft. We reviewed the DPA and the TOMs exhibit and highlighted three main blockers for our InfoSec team:

1) Cross-border transfers — Acme Health processes EU patient-contact data and we need clarity on transfer mechanism (standard contractual clauses + SCC II/III compatibility).
2) Subprocessors — request for 30-day notice before onboarding new subprocessors and a right to audit critical subprocessors.
3) Key management — we prefer Customer-Managed Keys (BYOK/KMS) for encryption at rest; if redwood cannot support BYOK for hosted deployments we need an explicit compensating control (HSM-backed key envelopes and annual key access review).

Attached are our redline comments (DPA_v3_redlines.pdf) and a marked-up TOMs exhibit (TOMs_Exhibit_v2.docx). Can your legal/security teams confirm which of these are acceptable? Also, are SCCs embedded in the DPA or do we need a separate addendum?

Best,
Sofia
InfoSec Program Manager
Acme Health

Sofia / Karen,

Thanks for the thorough review and the annotated TOMs — very helpful. Quick answers up-front and then next steps: 

- SCCs: We include the EU SCCs as Exhibit B of the DPA for transfers out of the EEA. We are tracking the applicability for SCC II/III and can add language that references latest European Commission guidance. If Acme prefers a standalone SCC addendum, we can provide that as well.

- Subprocessors: Redwood policy is 30-day notice for most subprocessors; for critical infra providers we currently notify at contract signature. For your request to have a formal right to audit we can offer a SOC2/SOC3 or ISO27001 report and a limited audit right scoped to the subprocessors that actually touch customer data (we typically limit to on-site or vendor-led audit with NDA and scheduling windows). Please confirm if that is sufficient.

- Key management / encryption: For hosted Redwood we offer two options: 1) Redwood-managed keys (AES-256, HSM-backed) with strict access controls and key-use logs; 2) Dedicated customers can supply KMS integration (customer-managed keys) for Dedicated/Private deployments. For the hosted API (your initial use case) we do not currently support BYOK. If BYOK is a mandatory requirement we recommend Dedicated capacity. Otherwise we can add the compensating control language you suggested (HSM key envelopes, quarterly key access reviews, and encryption-at-rest + in-transit AES/TLS v1.2+).

Next steps I suggest:
- Rishi (cc) to circulate a short TOMs redline that reflects the HSM/envelope compromise and the 30-day notice + SOC2 offering for subprocessors.
- Karen, if you can confirm whether Acme requires a standalone SCC addendum or will accept Exhibit B, we can prepare the countersigned DPA for e-signature.
- We can push to DocuSign once redlines are agreed; typical turnaround for execution is 2–3 business days.

I attached our internal redlined DPA and a comment summary (attached).

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Head of Partnerships (on rotation)
Redwood Inference

Folks — quick operational note from infra/security:

- Encryption details to include in TOMs: AES-256-GCM for data at rest, TLS 1.3 for in-transit, and KMIP-compatible HSM provider for key wrapping. We can add the following sentence to the TOMs: "Encryption at rest is performed using AES-256-GCM with keys stored in an HSM; key wrapping used for multi-tenant hosted storage is KMIP-compatible and access to raw keys is restricted to a small number of cryptographic service accounts with MFA and just-in-time access logs."

- Subprocessor audit: we can commit to providing yearly SOC2 reports for subprocessors and 30-day notice of new subprocessors. For critical subprocessors (defined as those storing or transmitting PHI/PII) we will provide a vendor security questionnaire and, upon mutual NDA, a scoped review.

- SCC approach: we'll include the clause that applies SCCs as Exhibit B and add a clause to automatically update to the latest SCC template adopted by the EU Commission. That should meet Acme's compliance team requirement without a separate addendum.

I attached a tight TOMs excerpt you can drop into your markup.

-Rishi
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Ava / Rishi / Team,

Thanks — Acme's counsel has reviewed Redwood's responses and the TOMs excerpt. Two remaining asks before legal is comfortable signing: 

1) Add an explicit statement that Redwoods will use the latest published EU SCCs automatically (we prefer a sentence rather than relying on Exhibit references).
2) For hosted deployments, carbon-copy the compensating-control language into Exhibit 1 (TOMs) AND add a monthly key-access report deliverable during the first year post-execution.

If Redwood can accept those two items we can proceed to DocuSign. Acme prefers DocuSign, but they can accept AdobeSign if your platform requires it. Please confirm e-signature provider and I'll circulate the DocuSign envelope to their legal team.

Karen Allen
Partner
Ellis & Partners — Privacy & Security Practice

Karen / Sofia — great, thanks for the clear asks. Confirmations and commit: 

- We will add an explicit sentence in the DPA body that Redwood will adopt the latest EU SCCs ("Redwood will implement the latest European Commission standard contractual clauses for transfers of personal data from the EEA to the United States as they are published, and the parties agree that such updated clauses will be deemed incorporated into this DPA").

- For hosted customers where BYOK is not enabled, we will add the compensating-control language directly into Exhibit 1 (TOMs) and commit to producing a monthly key-access report for the first 12 months after execution. After 12 months we'll revert to quarterly reporting unless otherwise agreed. The monthly report will be a redacted access report showing key usage metrics and the identity (service account id) of the principal requesting unwrap operations.

- DocuSign: Redwood prefers DocuSign for rapid turnaround. I will prepare the final countersigned DPA and push to DocuSign once you confirm and we'll include the attachments referenced in the thread. Expect an envelope link within 24 hours of confirmation.

If that works for Acme we'll finalize and execute.

Thanks,
